items.claim: Both of this row's seams are crossed by byte-true devices that go undisclosed, and its internal bounding device is tier-overstated and not local to the row.
items.evidence: FRONT SEAM (8:17|9:1): the row's own opening evidence is the heart-giving formula, and its verb is BYTE-IDENTICAL across that seam - נָתַ֤תִּי (oshb:Eccl.9.1, tier: byte) is the same bytes as נָתַ֤תִּי (oshb:Eccl.8.16, tier: byte); the pointed form byte-sweeps to 2 verses (MT 8:16, 9:1) and to 3 verses at accent_stripped/skeleton (adding MT 1:13). The full runs differ only in the preposition: נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.8.16, tier: byte) vs נָתַ֤תִּי אֶל לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.9.1, tier: byte) - same verb, same object - so the row opens on a formula it shares with the verse immediately before its front seam. Undisclosed. REAR SEAM (9:3|9:4): the love/hatred word-pair quoted as the row's thesis, גַּֽם אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם שִׂנְאָ֗ה (oshb:Eccl.9.1, tier: byte), returns as גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם (oshb:Eccl.9.6, tier: byte); those two lexemes co-occur in only 3 verses book-wide (skeleton sweeps: love-family 5 verses - MT 3:8, 5:9, 9:1, 9:6, 9:9; hate-family 7 verses - MT 2:17, 2:18, 3:8, 8:1, 9:1, 9:6, 9:12; intersection MT 3:8, 9:1, 9:6), so the row's thesis is one arm of a bracket that closes two verses PAST its rear seam. The death-token chain crosses the same seam: הַמֵּתִֽים (oshb:Eccl.9.3, tier: byte) recurs as וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים (oshb:Eccl.9.5, tier: byte) - that exact skeleton stands in only 3 verses book-wide (MT 4:2, 9:3, 9:5) - with הַמֵּֽת (oshb:Eccl.9.4, tier: byte) continuing it in between. Undisclosed. TIER OVER-CLAIM: the two one-event splices are each labelled tier: byte and called an echo word-for-word, but they are NOT byte-identical - מִקְרֶ֨ה אֶחָ֜ד (oshb:Eccl.9.2) byte-sweeps to 1 verse and מִקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד (oshb:Eccl.9.3) byte-sweeps to 1 verse; the echo holds only at accent_stripped (3 verses: MT 3:19, 9:2, 9:3) and skeleton (4 verses: MT 2:14, 3:19, 9:2, 9:3). Because the same phrase already stands at MT 2:14 and 3:19 it is a book-level fate refrain and cannot by itself carry bounding-device weight. QUOTE/GLOSS PARITY: the label deed-in-hand formula is attached to the clause whose Hebrew is נָתַ֤תִּי אֶל לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.9.1, tier: byte) - I gave to my heart - which carries no hand or deed lexeme; the hand token of MT 9:1 belongs to a different clause. CLEAN: the shin-dot oath form הַנִּשְׁבָּ֕ע (oshb:Eccl.9.2, tier: byte) sits inside the span but the row makes no three-way-homograph count, so that hazard is not tripped; the paseq seg at MT 9:3 is count-only and no position is asserted.

items.claim: The front-seam warrant is carried entirely by the English rendering and by a particle that is not distinctive in the Hebrew, while three byte-true devices cross this row's own seams undisclosed.
items.evidence: TRANSLATION-DEPENDENT WARRANT: the only front-seam grounds offered are a WEB quote and the English causal for. In the bytes that particle is not distinctive at this seam - MT 9:4 opens כִּי, MT 9:5 opens כִּ֧י, and the thesis clause of MT 9:3 is itself כִּֽי מִקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל (all tier: byte). No Hebrew form is quoted for the boundary itself, so the seam claim is not byte-engaged. FRONT SEAM CROSSED (9:3|9:4): הַמֵּתִֽים (oshb:Eccl.9.3, tier: byte) - הַמֵּֽת (oshb:Eccl.9.4, tier: byte) - וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים (oshb:Eccl.9.5, tier: byte) form an unbroken death-token chain over the seam; the exact plural skeleton stands in only 3 verses book-wide (MT 4:2, 9:3, 9:5). The row quotes the living/dead antithesis of MT 9:5 without noting that its second member is already in place in the verse before its own front seam. BRACKET IGNORED: the row's closing WEB quote renders גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם (oshb:Eccl.9.6, tier: byte), which answers גַּֽם אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם שִׂנְאָ֗ה (oshb:Eccl.9.1, tier: byte) - a love/hate pairing attested in only 3 verses book-wide (skeleton intersection: MT 3:8, 9:1, 9:6). That bracket spans MT 9:1-9:6 and argues those six verses cohere against the 9:3|9:4 cut. REAR SEAM CROSSED (9:6|9:7): וְחֵ֨לֶק (oshb:Eccl.9.6, tier: byte) is answered antithetically by חֶלְקְךָ֙ (oshb:Eccl.9.9, tier: byte) - the portion lexeme stands in 8 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: MT 2:10, 2:21, 3:22, 5:17, 5:18, 9:6, 9:9, 11:2) - and the under-the-sun refrain the row cites at MT 9:6 recurs at MT 9:9 and 9:11 (inventory: 27 verses book-wide, 5 of them in ch 9). Neither is disclosed. SOUND: the K/Q disclosure is exact - the unpointed ketiv stands inline before the pointed qere as יבחר יְחֻבַּ֔ר (oshb:Eccl.9.4, tier: byte), matching the 12-note MT-keyed inventory at MT 9:4, and it is correctly held as a textual feature rather than a boundary driver.

items.claim: Both seams are byte-marked - a second-person imperative register opens the unit and a byte-true two-root ring closes it - with the tier-3 setumah disclosed at the correct key and type.
items.evidence: FRONT SEAM (9:6|9:7): לֵ֣ךְ אֱכֹ֤ל בְּשִׂמְחָה֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Eccl.9.7, tier: byte) opens a run of second-person forms continued by יֵינֶ֑ךָ and מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ (oshb:Eccl.9.7, tier: byte), whereas the pronominal reference of MT 9:1-9:6 is uniformly third-person: לִפְנֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Eccl.9.1), בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Eccl.9.3), לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Eccl.9.5), לָהֶ֥ם (oshb:Eccl.9.6), all tier: byte. The register break is in the bytes, not only in the WEB rendering. REAR SEAM (9:10|9:11): the imperative bracket is byte-true and in fact tighter than claimed - the go-root rings the unit, לֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Eccl.9.7, tier: byte) closing as הֹלֵ֥ךְ שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Eccl.9.10, tier: byte), and the do-root closes over it, מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ (oshb:Eccl.9.7) answered by לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה (oshb:Eccl.9.10), both tier: byte. The next verse re-opens first-person narration with שַׁ֜בְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.9.11, tier: byte). MARKS: the setumah at MT 9:10 is disclosed at the row's own close under the correct type and MT key against the 4-seg inventory (1 PE at MT 1:11; SAMEKH at MT 3:1, 3:8, 9:10), tier-3 weak, single witness, and is used as corroboration rather than driver; no PE/SAMEKH conflation and no special-letter or selah claim anywhere in the row. NOTED, NOT CHALLENGE-GRADE: the following-verse warrant asserts a first-person retrospective form without quoting it or anchoring its ref; and the under-the-sun refrain stands on both sides of both seams (MT 9:6, 9:9, 9:11) undisclosed - it does not overturn a register break of this size, but it is the disclosure the standing cross-seam rule expects.
tier_citations: tier-3 SAMEKH at MT 9:10 (WLC single witness; 1 PE + 3 SAMEKH book-wide)

items.claim: The boundary holds, but the pairing of the two verses is argued only from the English while the Hebrew chain that actually binds them is never quoted, and the sweep digit's object is under-named.
items.evidence: TRANSLATION-DEPENDENT PAIRING: the only reason offered for holding the two verses together is an English restatement about time. The byte-true chain is not cited: עֵ֥ת (oshb:Eccl.9.11, tier: byte) is answered by the suffixed עִתּ֗וֹ and the prefixed לְעֵ֣ת (oshb:Eccl.9.12, tier: byte); the inventory's 8 word-bound time-form verses outside the catalogue include both MT 9:11 and 9:12, and MT 9:12 is the verse that uniquely carries two of them. The fate verb יִקְרֶ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.9.11, tier: byte) is also the same root as the one-event refrain of MT 9:2-9:3 that the cluster's opening row cites; that link goes unused. COUNT-OBJECT NAMING: the row splices the single pointed form שַׁ֜בְתִּי (oshb:Eccl.9.11, tier: byte) and attaches (sweep: 3 verses) to such turns. The digit verifies, but only for the two attested spellings taken together (skeleton sweep: 3 verses - MT 4:1, 4:7, 9:11; MT 9:11 carries the bare form, MT 4:1 and 4:7 the waw-prefixed one); a reader sweeping the pointed splice as printed gets 1 verse, so the swept object is under-named against the spelling-versus-term discipline. REAR SEAM CROSSED: the under-the-sun refrain stands at תַֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.9.11, tier: byte) and again at תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ (oshb:Eccl.9.13, tier: byte), and the wisdom root runs לַחֲכָמִ֥ים (oshb:Eccl.9.11) to חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.13), both tier: byte, across the row's own rear seam; the following-unit warrant names an observation formula without quoting it or anchoring its ref. SOUND: the front-seam setumah disclosure at MT 9:10 is correct in type, key and tier (tier-3 weak, WLC single witness), and the discourse pivot at MT 9:11 is a real byte-attested opener.

items.claim: The rear seam is the one cut in this cluster the bytes actively contest, and the disclosure omits a book-unique catchword pair, a second repeated lexeme, and a byte-identical phrase frame across it.
items.evidence: BOOK-UNIQUE CATCHWORD ACROSS THE ROW'S OWN REAR SEAM: נִשְׁמָעִֽים (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte) and נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) are the ONLY two verses in the book carrying that skeleton (skeleton sweep: 2 verses - MT 9:16, 9:17). The words lexeme repeats over the same seam: וּדְבָרָ֖יו (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte) against דִּבְרֵ֣י (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) (skeleton sweep: 14 verses book-wide). Two repeated lexemes on an adjacent pair, one of them book-unique, is the strongest cohesion signal anywhere in this cluster, and it is not disclosed. BYTE-IDENTICAL FRAME STRADDLING THE SEAM: the row's own closing judgment opens טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte), and MT 9:18 opens with the SAME BYTES, טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) - that pointed two-token run byte-sweeps to 3 verses book-wide (MT 7:11, 9:16, 9:18). The row therefore places its seam inside a byte-identical frame whose two arms are its own last verse and the verse after next. TRANSLATION-SHAPED REASON: the stated ground turns on an English theme contrast (wisdom-despised versus wisdom-praised) plus the genitive-versus-header point. The genitive point is correct against the inventory (4 verse-initial sites, only MT 1:1 a header), but it does not answer the lexical evidence: the wisdom root runs unbroken at MT 9:13, 9:15, 9:16, 9:17, 9:18 and 10:1 (skeleton sweep: 32 verses book-wide), so register alone does not separate the anecdote's conclusion from what follows. CREDIT: the opening splice גַּם זֹ֛ה רָאִ֥יתִי חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.13, tier: byte) and the narrator's comment וְאָמַ֣רְתִּי אָ֔נִי (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte) are both accurate, and holding the row in a lower confidence band with the rival named is honest - but the rival is stated on the weakest available grounds while the byte-grounded version of it is omitted.

items.claim: The rejected alternative rests on two premises the bytes contradict: this verse carries no tov element at all, and its front seam does carry repeated lexemes.
items.evidence: NO TOV ELEMENT IN THIS VERSE: the row rejects clustering with the following verse on the shared tov-comparative form, but MT 9:17 carries no good-token of any form - the skeleton sweep of the feminine spelling returns 9 verses (MT 4:8, 5:10, 5:17, 6:3, 6:6, 7:11, 7:14, 9:16, 9:18) and MT 9:17 is not among them, and the inventory's 12 tov-opener verses likewise exclude it. The comparison in MT 9:17 is carried by the bare mem-prefix of מִזַּעֲקַ֥ת (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) with no good-element present, so the rival being rejected is a construction this verse does not have. REPEATED LEXEMES DO STAND AT THE SEAM: the assertion that the paired verses share no repeated lexeme is aimed in the wrong direction - the byte-true rival is cohesion with the PRECEDING verse, not the following one: נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) repeats נִשְׁמָעִֽים (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte), a skeleton attested in only 2 verses book-wide (MT 9:16, 9:17), and דִּבְרֵ֣י (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) repeats וּדְבָרָ֖יו (oshb:Eccl.9.16, tier: byte). That rival is never engaged. Even toward the following verse the wisdom root is shared (MT 9:17 חֲכָמִ֔ים against MT 9:18 חָכְמָ֖ה, both tier: byte), so a flat no-shared-lexeme claim is contestable in both directions. SOUND: the opening splice דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים בְּנַ֖חַת נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.9.17, tier: byte) is accurate, the genitive-not-header reading matches the inventory (4 verse-initial sites, only MT 1:1 header-functioning), and the single_saying verdict itself survives under the sentence-zone default - the defect is the warrant, not the unit.
tier_citations: sweep: 9 verses skeleton (feminine good-token; MT 9:17 absent)

items.claim: The row's substrate signal states the opposite of the bytes about this verse's opening token, and its rejected alternative denies a lexeme that demonstrably repeats across the chapter seam.
items.evidence: SUBSTRATE SIGNAL INVERTED: the row records that the tov-opener set does not include this verse, but MT 9:18's FIRST token is טוֹבָ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) and the inventory's 12-verse tov-opener list contains MT 9:18. The row's own prose simultaneously calls the verse a tov-comparative, so the dependent field contradicts both the bytes and the row's own reading. The construction claim itself is right and is exactly the phrase-extension case: the mem-token does not stand adjacent to the good-token, which is why the 6-verse contiguous adjacency set (MT 3:22, 4:3, 4:6, 6:3, 6:9, 9:4) excludes MT 9:18. REPEATED LEXEME DENIED: the rejected alternative says this verse and the next share no repeated lexeme. They share the wisdom noun: חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) recurs with a comparative mem as מֵחָכְמָ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte); the skeleton sweep of that lexeme returns 22 verses book-wide with both MT 9:18 and MT 10:1 among them, and per the contained-substring hazard all 22 hits are wisdom-family tokens, so the hit is real and not a short-token artefact. Both verses are also mem-comparatives with the same little-outweighs-much shape: וְחוֹטֶ֣א אֶחָ֔ד יְאַבֵּ֥ד טוֹבָ֥ה הַרְבֵּֽה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) against מֵחָכְמָ֥ה מִכָּב֖וֹד סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte). UNDISCLOSED FRAME: this verse's opening run טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) is byte-identical to MT 9:16's (byte sweep: 3 verses - MT 7:11, 9:16, 9:18), so the verse is the second arm of a byte-identical frame around MT 9:17; not disclosed. The single_saying verdict survives under the zone default - the defects are in the warrant and in the dependent field.
tier_citations: inventory: 6 contiguous tov-mem adjacency verses (MT 9:18 absent)

items.claim: The verdict stands but its stated ground is byte-false - the wisdom lexeme does repeat across the chapter seam - and the verse's image half is engaged only through the English.
items.evidence: BYTE-FALSE GROUND: the rejected alternative is dismissed for want of any repeated lexeme between the two verses, yet מֵחָכְמָ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte) is the wisdom noun of MT 9:18, חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte), carrying a comparative mem; the skeleton sweep returns 22 verses book-wide including both, and the contained-substring hazard is not in play because every hit is a wisdom-family token. The shared material goes further than the lexeme: both verses are mem-comparatives built on a little-versus-much antithesis - וְחוֹטֶ֣א אֶחָ֔ד יְאַבֵּ֥ד טוֹבָ֥ה הַרְבֵּֽה (oshb:Eccl.9.18, tier: byte) against מֵחָכְמָ֥ה מִכָּב֖וֹד סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte). ENGAGEMENT: the row's only Hebrew is the two-token splice סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte) from the verse's final clause; the image half on which the row rests its image-maxim reading, זְב֣וּבֵי מָ֔וֶת יַבְאִ֥ישׁ יַבִּ֖יעַ שֶׁ֣מֶן רוֹקֵ֑חַ (oshb:Eccl.10.1, tier: byte), is argued only from the WEB rendering, so that form claim rests on the translation. SOUND: the splice collates at byte tier against its cited ref, no fabricated mark or special-letter claim appears, and the single_saying verdict is defensible on its own terms - MT 10:1 is one syntactically complete image-maxim and the sentence-zone default governs. The catchword-adjacency figure quoted for the chapter matches the staging inventory (3 of 19 adjacent pairs), though that is a heuristic staging signal and is leaned on here as corroboration for the unit decision.
